clue.text: Big wheels of finest metal

blocks.note: the top grade is the finest
brass is an alloy metal

explanation.surface: Important people turned out in the finest metals, like a medal display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big wheels' looks mechanical, but it is slang for important people.
explanation.definitionFit: TOP BRASS is an idiom for the senior officers or bosses, the same people called big wheels.

clue.text: Take care of deer and lion, say, from the south

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from the south means reading upwards, bottom to top

blocks.note: the elk is a large deer
the lion is a big cat; 'say' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: Someone looks after a deer and a lion that came up from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you lion is one example of the wider word wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle a job is to deal with it, so it can mean take care of.

clue.text: See 10
Radioactive gas unsettled NORAD

indicators.note: something unsettled is disturbed out of its place, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the five letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A leak of radioactive gas has rattled the North American air defence command.
explanation.walkthrough: NORAD is the North American Aerospace Defense Command.
explanation.definitionFit: Radon is a noble gas that is radioactive, element 86.

clue.text: Defence against main onslaught?

blocks.note: surface reading: protection against the chief attack in a war
setter's reading: the main is an old poetic word for the ocean, so this is a barrier against the waves

explanation.walkthrough: 'main' reads as chief, but in poetry the main is the open ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: This barrier is built along a coast to protect land from the force of the waves.

clue.text: Country staff employed for a spell in R&A

indicators.note: the golf club's letters sit on either side, so the staff word goes inside them

blocks.note: the Royal and Ancient golf club, taken letter by letter
a magic wand is a staff used to cast spells

explanation.surface: A golf club's staff are working in Africa for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: The R&A is the Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews; 'for a spell' looks like 'for a while' but means magic.
explanation.definitionFit: Rwanda is a nation in central Africa.

clue.text: Several overcome by river current like bore?

indicators.note: in a down clue, being overcome means lying underneath, so the word for several comes last

blocks.note: the Wear is a river in north-east England
I is the symbol for electric current
some means a few, several

explanation.surface: A tidal bore is described as a river current overwhelming several things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' and 'river current' suggest a tidal wave; here bore means a tedious person.
explanation.definitionFit: A bore is tiresome company, so wearisome describes what a bore is like.

clue.text: Old tools from Holstein reused

indicators.note: something reused is put to a different purpose, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Ancient implements recycled from the German region of Holstein.
explanation.definitionFit: Neoliths are stone implements from the New Stone Age, so old tools.

clue.text: Is a Tudor playing checkers?

indicators.note: playing a role means taking another form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A question about whether a Tudor monarch is playing the board game checkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'checkers' looks like the board game, but it means people who check.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditors inspect accounts, so they are financial checkers.

clue.text: North American daughter, one in Biblical land

indicators.note: the letters of daughter and one go inside the land, splitting it

blocks.note: Canaan is the promised land of the Bible
standard abbreviation for daughter
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A daughter from North America is the one living in the Holy Land.
explanation.walkthrough: Canaan is the land promised to Abraham in Genesis; the inserted letters split it after its fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Canadian is a person from Canada, a nation of North America.

clue.text: Dramatist rather oddly grabs antique brooch

indicators.note: done oddly means done in a strange way, so the letters of the word before are rearranged
something that grabs another holds it within its grasp

blocks.note: the six letters of this word, rearranged
antiques are old
a brooch is a decorative pin

explanation.surface: A playwright somewhat strangely snatches an old brooch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' tempts you to take alternate letters of rather, but here it signals a rearrangement of the whole word.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Pinter was a Nobel-winning English playwright, author of The Birthday Party.

clue.text: Estonian regularly eschewed hot spot

indicators.note: dropping at regular intervals means every other letter is skipped

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: An Estonian habitually avoided a warm resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is an active volcano in Sicily, a literally hot spot.

clue.text: Prepare to catch Spooner's reason for delayed arrival at work?

indicators.note: named after Reverend Spooner, who swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.clueFragment: reason for delayed arrival at work?
blocks.note: the question asked of a latecomer; swap the opening sounds of the first and last words

explanation.surface: A boss asks for the reason someone turned up late to work.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue phrase is really the question 'Why in late?', which with W and L swapped becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie in wait is to stay hidden ready to ambush, that is, to get ready to catch someone.

clue.text: Dunce! I had nothing invested in it

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it

blocks.note: contracted to I'd
taken as written
zero, shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: Someone admits they were a fool to put no money into a venture.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation 'Dunce!' sounds like self-reproach, but it is simply the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce and an idiot are both synonyms for a stupid person.

clue.text: First victim: president after James B?

blocks.note: first meaning: the son of Adam murdered by his brother Cain, the first killing in Genesis
second meaning, punning: James Buchanan was followed by Abraham Lincoln

explanation.walkthrough: James B is James Buchanan; the next president was Abe Lincoln, which with his surname cut to its initial reads as the answer, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible Abel is the first person ever killed, slain by Cain.

clue.text: Tory wife, fit, big swimmer

blocks.note: blue is the colour of the Conservatives, so a Tory is a blue
standard abbreviation for wife
hale means healthy and fit

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician's wife is fit and a strong swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for Britain's Conservative Party, whose colour is blue.
explanation.definitionFit: This animal is the largest creature ever known, and it swims in the ocean.

clue.text: One more circle inside flower part

indicators.note: the circle is placed within the flower part, enclosed by it

blocks.note: the anther is the pollen-bearing part of a stamen
a circle is shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: A botanist spots yet another ring in a flower's structure.
explanation.definitionFit: Another means an additional one, a synonym for one more.

clue.text: Got drunk into a bed

indicators.note: someone drunk staggers about out of order, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone got so drunk they fell into a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got drunk' reads as one phrase, but 'Got' is the definition and 'drunk' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtained is a synonym for got, both in the past tense of acquiring.

clue.text: Secured loan bank brought in without interest?

indicators.note: something brought in is taken inside another thing

blocks.note: a person with no interest in something is bored
a bank of keys or seats is a row

explanation.surface: A loan from a bank that charges no interest has been secured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' and 'interest' pretend to be finance; bank is a row and 'without interest' means uninterested.
explanation.definitionFit: To have borrowed is to have obtained a loan, so it is a fair swap for secured loan.

clue.text: Book, woeful novel, work in Old English

indicators.note: novel means new and different, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for book
these six letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: A literary critic calls an Old English book a dismal novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' and 'novel' sound like the subject of the clue, but they are a letter and an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Beowulf is the famous epic poem written in Old English, the language of Anglo-Saxon England.

clue.text: Obese English lot

blocks.note: obese means very fat
standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A grim comment on the overweight English people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lot' looks like a quantity, but it means one's destiny.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot in life is one's destiny, a synonym for fate.

clue.text: Meat and bone to pick

blocks.note: first meaning: flesh from cattle
second meaning: a grievance or complaint

explanation.walkthrough: Meat and bone sit together like a butcher's order; 'a bone to pick' is an idiom for a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is cow meat, and also slang for a grudge or complaint someone has with another.

clue.text: Act as minder for small charge?

definitions.text: Act as minder for small charge?

blocks.clueFragment: Act as minder for small charge?
blocks.note: surface reading: do a supervisory job for a low fee
setter's reading: the charge is a little child placed in your care

explanation.walkthrough: 'small charge' reads as a modest price, but a charge is also someone in your care.
explanation.definitionFit: To do this is to look after a young child while the parents are out.

clue.text: Tolkien character touring a Spanish city

indicators.note: touring means going around, so one word wraps around another

blocks.note: Bilbo Baggins is the hobbit of Tolkien's tale
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hobbit goes on tour around a Spanish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilbao is the largest city of the Basque Country in northern Spain.

clue.text: Singular odds for a kind of rugby

blocks.note: grammatical abbreviation for singular
evens are betting odds of one to one

explanation.surface: A bookmaker quotes unusual odds on a rugby match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular odds' reads as strange odds; 'odds' giving the word for its opposite is a neat twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Sevens is a fast form of rugby union played with seven players a side.

clue.text: Posh school fails to open – one in the eye for 10?

indicators.note: failing to open means the opening letter is missing

blocks.note: Harrow is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: An elite school's opening goes badly, a real blow for the dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is HAROLD, and King Harold was said to be killed by one shot into his eye at Hastings in 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says King Harold died from an arrow in the eye, so the missile is literally one in his eye.

clue.text: Arrived unexpectedly going among Scots to drink

indicators.note: going among something means passing into the middle of it

blocks.note: tae is the Scots form of the word to
to blow in is to turn up without warning

explanation.surface: Someone turned up out of the blue among Scottish people to have a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scots to' means the Scots word for to, not a group of Scots; 'to drink' looks like a purpose but 'drink' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Table wine is ordinary wine served with meals, a type of drink.

clue.text: European clubs in black turn out

indicators.note: the clubs letter is placed inside the word for black

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for European
jet is a deep black
the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: European nightclubs throw people out while dressed in black.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject someone is to throw them out, which is what turn out means here.

clue.text: Cardinal a reformed character?

blocks.note: first meaning: John Henry, the Victorian churchman made a cardinal and later a saint
second meaning, split in two: someone changed for the better

explanation.walkthrough: Cardinal is not a number or a bird here but a Catholic prince; read the answer as two words for the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: John Henry Newman was an English cardinal, and a 'new man' is someone who has reformed.

clue.text: Come together – see lambs frolicking

indicators.note: frolicking animals leap about playfully, so the letters jump into a new order

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An invitation to gather and watch young sheep at play.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble is to gather, a synonym for come together.

clue.text: Shirker in Kansas City – right!

blocks.note: Dodge City is a town in Kansas
standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone confirms that the idler lives in a city in Kansas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kansas City' tempts as the big city of that name, but it is the Wild West town Dodge City.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodger avoids work or duty, just as a shirker does.

clue.text: Stops one working in facts and figures

indicators.note: the worker goes inside the short word for statistics

blocks.note: stats is short for statistics
the Roman numeral for one
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Someone halts a person employed in compiling statistics.
explanation.definitionFit: Stations are the regular stopping places on a railway or bus line.
